title: Comparing membranes and bone substitutes in a one-stage procedure for horizontal bone augmentation. A double-blind randomized controlled trial
authors: Merli M, Moscatelli M, Mariotti G, Pagliaro U, Raffaelli E, Nieri M., Eur J Oral Implantol. 2015; 8(3):271-81.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “No significant differences, except for radiographic bone loss, were observed in this randomized controlled trial comparing anorganic bovine bone with collagen porcine membranes versus synthetic resorbable bone made of pure β -tricalcium phosphate with peri cardium collagen membranes for horizontal augmentation” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
